newsitem.title: USA: Aid Auto sees improvements ahead.
newsitem.headline: Aid Auto sees improvements ahead.

text.p: Aid Auto Stores Inc Friday reported a first quarter loss saying it sees improved results in upcoming quarters.
Revenues were $6.1 million for the quarter compared to $6.6 million a year earlier. The per share net loss was $0.01 compared to net income of $0.01 per share for the comparable year ago period.
The decline in revenues was attributable in part to the company's continued de-emphasis of its franchise business, it said.
Through termination and non-renewal of franchise agreements, the number of franchised stores has decreased since the end of the first quarter of 1996 to 34 from 43.

Sales on both the retail and wholesale levels were hurt by unseasonably mild weather in the first quarter, traditionally the weakest quarter, it said. Mild weather resulted in the reduced sale of products such as antifreeze, car batteries, windshield washer fluid, ice scrapers and snowbrushes.
The company is pleased with its strategic redirection to a retail operations, chief executive Philip L. Stephen said.

"Although our de-emphasis of wholesale operations and unseasonable weather resulted in a decline in overall sales, sales from our retail operations continue to grow nicely. In addition, retail operations resulted in improved gross margins from 39 percent to 42 percent and our attention to cost was successful as ... expenses remained relatively flat despite an increase in company-owned store count."

He said, "We expect that our continued focus on retail operations will result in a significant improvement in financial results in upcoming periods. The company also continues to evaluate potential acquisitions as well as innovative retailing strategies."

The company is engaged in "negotiations with a large regional retailer with respect to opening mini-Aid Auto Stores within the retailer's stores. The 'Aid' mini-stores would carry fast-moving auto parts in addition to the automotive chemicals, accessories and tools found in some other non-automotive retailers," Stephen said.

He said a successful launch of this "Aid" mini-store program could result in significant increases in the number of Aid Auto retail locations, complementing the company's Superstore program and enhancing brand recognition."
